title.narrative: Provision of Life-Saving WASH, Health and Nutrition Assistance for Vulnerable and Conflict-Affected Populations in Dikwa, Ngala and Magumeri LGAs, Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtLife at Best Development Initiative (LABDI), in consortium with Sorasun Foundation (SRF) and Multi Aid and Charity Initiative (MACI), proposes a six-month integrated Health, Nutrition, and WASH intervention under the NHF Lean-Season Standard Allocation to address urgent humanitarian needs in Ngala, Dikwa, and Magumeri LGAs of Borno State. The project targets ltbrgt17,576 vulnerable individuals—IDPs, returnees, and host communities—with a holistic package that reduces morbidity and mortality, strengthens community systems, and mitigates the effects of conflict and seasonal disease outbreaks.ltbrgtThe Health component will enhance both facility and mobile service delivery. 1 primary health facility in Ngala LGA will provide essential services including outpatient consultations (OPD), Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMNCI), Sexual and Reproductive Health (SRH) with BEmONC, maternal and newborn care, immunization (EPI), and management of non-communicable diseases (NCDs). 3 Mobile Medical Teams (MMTs) will serve hard-to-reach areas with OPD, ANC/PNC, disease surveillance, and health promotion. Epidemic-prone disease surveillance and rapid response will be strengthened for cholera, measles, diphtheria, and meningitis, supported by infection prevention and control (IPC), WASH in health facilities, and immunization campaigns.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe Nutrition component in Dikwa LGA will focus on early detection and management of acute malnutrition among children 6–59 months and Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW). Community Nutrition Mobilizers (CNMs) will conduct MUAC screening, Vitamin A supplementation, deworming, and Maternal, Infant, and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counselling through Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC). Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) will be referred for TSFP services, while Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) cases will be enrolled in OTPs and referred to Stabilization Centres (SCs) for inpatient care. Capacity building for frontline health workers will strengthen IYCF counselling, SAM management, and referral coordination across all levels.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe WASH component, implemented by LABDI in Magumeri, will ensure sustainable access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene. Activities include rehabilitation of solar-powered water systems, chlorination points, and gender-segregated latrines desludging, waste management, and canal cleaning to prevent contamination. Households will receive WASH NFIs (soap, jerry cans, aqua tabs) and benefit from hygiene promotion and cholera prevention campaigns aligned with Health and Nutrition messaging.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProtection, Gender, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and disability inclusion will be mainstreamed across all activities. Community sessions will integrate GBV risk mitigation, PSEA awareness, and Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) on hygiene, disease prevention, and reproductive health. Updated GBV referral pathways will ensure survivors’ safe access to specialized services, while help desks, suggestion boxes, and toll-free lines will strengthen feedback and accountability.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project contributes to NHF Lean-Season Allocation objectives by reducing under-five and maternal morbidity and mortality, improving early malnutrition management, expanding access to safe water and sanitation, reducing cholera and AWD incidence, and promoting gender-responsive, accountable, and integrated service delivery at community and facility levels.ltbrgtlt/pgt
